result.summary:
FAIL. docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-028.md (commit b7191cb, branch feature/WF02-REQ-028) describes 5 new verification cases as already-existing, already-committed vitest code in a 'new committed file, apps/bot/src/handlers/checkin.forgery.test.ts' -- but that file does not exist anywhere in this repository's history. `git log --all --oneline -- apps/bot/src/handlers/checkin.forgery.test.ts` returns nothing; `find apps/bot/src -iname '*forgery*'` finds only the unrelated apps/bot/src/handlers/reminder24h.forgery.test.ts (REQ-026); `git show b7191cb --stat` shows the commit touched only docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-028.md (327 lines) and handoffs/WF02-REQ-028/step-03-test-designer.json (30 lines) -- zero lines of test code. `git status --short` on the branch is clean, so nothing is sitting uncommitted either.

This is not a wording nitpick: the spec's own text asserts fabricated facts as already true. Verbatim from the spec: 'Per this run's task brief, every case below is this spec's own, independently designed, in a second new committed file, apps/bot/src/handlers/checkin.forgery.test.ts' (line 16-17); every one of the 5 case sections opens with 'New `it(...)` in the new committed file' as though the code already exists; the tg_id-range paragraph claims 'confirmed distinct via grep -rn "nextTgId = " apps/bot/src' against a file that was never created for that grep to match. The Step 3 handoff (handoffs/WF02-REQ-028/step-03-test-designer.json) repeats the same claim in its own summary ('own nextTgId=920_000_000+ range, confirmed distinct via grep...against every existing file's range') and even lists specific fixture/assertion details (12-attendee/2-page split, 4-point header sequence, exact audit-row entityId checks) narrated as verified code behavior, none of which was ever written or run.

Re-derived independently, not taken on the producer's word: read apps/bot/src/handlers/checkin.ts and apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts in full for the technical content the spec is based on (toggleCheckIn's `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` inside db.transaction, decideCheckinToggleOutcome's pure decision table, makeCheckinToggleCallbackHandler's fresh getEventIdForRegistration-derived re-authorization, makeCheckinPageCallbackHandler's independent re-authorization and full re-render). The underlying reasoning the spec narrates about these code paths is technically sound (see result.evidence below) -- that is not in dispute. What fails this gate is that the spec claims a concrete, runnable artifact exists to exercise that reasoning, and it does not. Per Step 3b check (c) ('each case is precise enough to run without judgment') and the workflow's own purpose (TEST-RUNNER must be able to follow the spec mechanically), a case pointing at a nonexistent file is not runnable at all -- TEST-RUNNER would open apps/bot/src/handlers/checkin.forgery.test.ts, find nothing, and be unable to execute a single one of the 5 new cases. Coverage for AC1's page-turn interleaving, AC3's no-profiles-row fixture, AC4's toggle-driven counter sequence, the cross-event forged-toggle regression, and the concurrent double-toggle race remains exactly zero -- identical to before this step ran, despite the spec's and handoff's claim of having closed those gaps.

Secondary, contingent on how rework resolves this: TEST-DESIGNER's own role file (.claude/agents/test-designer.md) authorizes writing 'docs/agents/test-specs/<REQ-ID>.md' only -- it does not authorize producing or committing implementation/test code. This project's own precedent (apps/bot/src/handlers/reminder24h.forgery.test.ts, REQ-026) shows *.forgery.test.ts files are written and committed by BACKEND-DEV as part of the Step 2 feat commit, not by TEST-DESIGNER at Step 3. If that precedent holds here, the spec's premise -- narrating cases as already-committed TEST-DESIGNER-authored code -- is structurally wrong regardless of whether the file gets created, and ORCH needs to decide (and record, if this is a genuine role-boundary ambiguity per core-directives.md's decision-record process) whether TEST-DESIGNER is now expected to author committed vitest files for bot requirements, or whether this spec must be rewritten as a checklist routed back through BACKEND-DEV for implementation before TEST-RUNNER can execute it.

checks.every_ac_has_a_case: Nominally yes on paper -- AC1/AC3/AC4/cross-event-forgery/concurrent-toggle each have a described case, AC2/AC5/AC6 are explicitly deferred to BACKEND-DEV's already-committed checkin.db.test.ts cases (verified separately below). FAILS in substance because the 5 new cases point at a file that does not exist.
checks.no_todo_left: PASS in isolation (grep -in TODO on the spec: zero matches) -- irrelevant given the file-existence failure.
checks.cases_precise_and_runnable: FAIL. Each of the 5 new cases names an exact fixture, exact dispatch sequence, and exact pass/fail assertions -- the prose precision itself is good -- but every one targets code in apps/bot/src/handlers/checkin.forgery.test.ts, which does not exist in the working tree or in git history at any commit on this branch. A case cannot be 'run without judgment' when there is nothing to run.
checks.backend_dev_ac2_ac5_ac6_deferral_spot_ch: Independently confirmed apps/bot/src/handlers/checkin.db.test.ts exists and is committed (19186cd, amended 0eaa83a) -- this part of the spec's independence claim is accurate; the deferral to BACKEND-DEV's existing AC2/AC5/AC6 cases is legitimate and not itself a defect.
checks.technical_content_re_derivation: The reasoning the spec is built on was independently re-checked against the real implementation and holds: (1) AC1 -- makeCheckinPageCallbackHandler (checkin.ts) re-renders via buildCheckinView but the toggle button's callback_data is always exactly `checkin:toggle:<registrationId>` (renderCheckinListMessage) with no admission/eventId snapshot ever encoded in it, so an intervening page-turn genuinely does not close or refresh the staleness window toggleCheckIn's fresh FOR UPDATE read depends on. (2) toggleCheckIn (registration.ts ~944-1000) opens db.transaction, does `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`, decides via the pure decideCheckinToggleOutcome, then conditionally writes + exactly one writeAuditLog call per branch, matching the spec's description. (3) No isolationLevel override exists in this codebase, so Postgres's default READ COMMITTED applies, and the concurrent-double-toggle trace (second transaction blocks on the row lock, then re-reads the now-committed row, correctly re-derives 'undo') is consistent with the code as written -- this is a genuinely deterministic final state (checkedInAt === null), not dispatch-order-dependent, given both toggles target the SAME registration and toggleCheckIn's only I/O before the lock is the lock-acquiring SELECT itself.

issues: BLOCKING: docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-028.md and handoffs/WF02-REQ-028/step-03-test-designer.json both assert apps/bot/src/handlers/checkin.forgery.test.ts is an already-committed file containing 5 new vitest cases (AC1 page-turn interleaving, AC3 no-profiles-row, AC4 counter sequence, cross-event forged toggle, concurrent double-toggle). The file does not exist anywhere in git history on this branch (`git log --all -- apps/bot/src/handlers/checkin.forgery.test.ts` empty) and `git show b7191cb --stat` shows only the .md spec and handoff JSON were added. All 5 new cases are unrunnable as written; the coverage gaps they claim to close (most notably the cross-event forged-toggle regression, which SECURITY-REVIEWER's own ad hoc test was explicitly reverted) remain fully open.

MINOR (role-boundary ambiguity, flag for ORCH per core-directives.md instruction precedence): TEST-DESIGNER's role file authorizes writing the markdown spec only, not committing test code -- yet this project's own precedent (reminder24h.forgery.test.ts, REQ-026) has *.forgery.test.ts files authored by BACKEND-DEV during Step 2, not by TEST-DESIGNER at Step 3. Rework should either produce the missing file consistent with an ORCH-clarified role assignment, or rewrite the spec to stop narrating unwritten code as already committed and route actual authorship to the correct role before this gate can re-run.
